security_spec.violation_condition: In OpenSBI HSM suspend/resume, failing to save and restore mcountinhibit on a per-hart basis when mcycle is shared between harts on the same core, causing writes to mcountinhibit.CY from one hart's resume path to corrupt another hart's counter inhibit state.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: mcountinhibit save/restore missing or not per-hart in HSM suspend/resume flow; CSR write to mcountinhibit without checking hart-sharing of mcycle.CY
security_spec.summary: mcountinhibit.CY is shared between harts sharing mcycle; OpenSBI must save/restore mcountinhibit per-hart during HSM suspend/resume to avoid cross-hart counter inhibit corruption.

findings.finding: mcountinhibit CSR is not saved in the HSM non-retentive suspend save path. On resume, sbi_hart_reinit() -> mstatus_init() unconditionally writes 0xFFFFFFF8 to CSR_MCOUNTINHIBIT at lib/sbi/sbi_hart.c:65. Per the RISC-V spec (norm:mcountinhibit_cy_shared), mcountinhibit.CY is shared between harts on the same core when mcycle is shared. Writing 0xFFFFFFF8 (which sets CY=0, enabling mcycle) during one hart's resume corrupts the mcountinhibit.CY state of sibling harts that may have had CY=1 (inhibited) for profiling or power optimization. The saved CSR set (mie, mip, medeleg, mideleg, menvcfg) should also include mcountinhibit.

spec_citations.excerpt: The mcycle CSR may be shared between harts on the same core, in which case the mcountinhibit.CY field is also shared between those harts, and so writes to mcountinhibit.CY will be visible to those harts.

findings.finding: mstatus_init() unconditionally writes 0xFFFFFFF8 (CY=0, IR=0, HPMn=1) to CSR_MCOUNTINHIBIT on both cold and warm boot (including resume from non-retentive suspend). This is the write that triggers the cross-hart corruption when mcycle is shared: a hart resuming from suspend overwrites mcountinhibit.CY to 0 (enabled) on the shared register, corrupting the inhibit state of any sibling hart that had explicitly set CY=1. The warm-boot resume path should restore mcountinhibit to a saved per-hart value rather than writing a hardcoded default.

spec_citations.excerpt: The mcycle CSR may be shared between harts on the same core, in which case the mcountinhibit.CY field is also shared between those harts, and so writes to mcountinhibit.CY will be visible to those harts.
